'''9801''' ('''nine thousand eight hundred [and] one''') is the [[natural number]] following 9800 and preceding 9802.

== In mathematics ==
9801 is most notable for being the third, and only 4-digit [[square pentagonal number]],<ref>{{cite OEIS|A036353|Square pentagonal numbers.}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |last=Weisstein |first=Eric W. |title=Pentagonal Square Number |url=https://mathworld.wolfram.com/PentagonalSquareNumber.html |access-date=2026-08-05 |website=mathworld.wolfram.com |language=en}}</ref> since 9801 is a [[square number]], which can be written as: <math>99^2</math>, and it is also a [[pentagonal number]], since it can also be written as: <math>\frac{81\cdot(3\cdot81-1)}{2} = \frac{81\cdot242}{2}</math>.<ref>{{cite book |last1=Çevik |first1=Mehmet |title=On Triangular Pentagonal and Square Pentagonal  Numbers |date=2024-08-20 |publisher=Duvar Yayınları |isbn=978-625-6069-53-4 |page=53 |url=https://www.researchgate.net/profile/Mehmet-Cevik-7/publication/383254530_Scientific_Research_Reports-20240820-ISBN_978-625-6069-53-4/links/67aee67396e7fb48b9c17c80/Scientific-Research-Reports-20240820-ISBN-978-625-6069-53-4.pdf#page=52 |access-date=2026-08-06}}</ref> 9801 is also the number that is below [[10,000]] which are [[Reverse divisible number|integral multiples of their reversals]].{{efn|It is also known as a palintiple.<ref name="A031877" /><ref>{{citation|last = Holt |first = Benjamin V.|journal = Integers|mr = 3256704|page = A42| title = Some general results and open questions on palintiple numbers|url = http://www.emis.de/journals/INTEGERS/papers/o42/o42.Abstract.html|volume = 14|year = 2014}}.</ref>}} The only other number which has this property is 8712.<ref>{{Cite journal |last=Weisgerber |first=Simon |date=2024-02-14 |title=Value Judgments in Mathematics: G. H. Hardy and the (Non-)seriousness of Mathematical Theorems |url=https://doi.org/10.1007/s10516-023-09705-y |journal=Global Philosophy |volume=34 |issue=1 |pages=1 |doi=10.1007/s10516-023-09705-y |issn=2948-1538 |pmc=10878122}}</ref><ref>{{cite web |first=Erich |last=Friedman |title=What's Special About This Number?|url=https://erich-friedman.github.io/numbers.html |access-date=2026-08-07}}</ref><ref name="A031877">{{cite OEIS|A031877|Nontrivial reversal numbers (numbers which are integer multiples of their reversals), excluding palindromic numbers and multiples of 10.}}</ref> 9801 is the sixth number such as the [[binomial coefficient]]{{efn|Which is: <math>\frac{n}{2} </math><ref name="TFN" />}} is a [[square number|perfect square]].<ref name="TFN">{{Cite book |last=Koninck |first=J. M. de |url=http://archive.org/details/thosefascinating0000koni |title=Those fascinating numbers |date=2009 |publisher=Providence, R.I. : American Mathematical Society |others=Internet Archive |isbn=978-0-8218-4807-4}}</ref> 9801 is a part of one of the first few pairs of consecutive [[powerful numbers]] with 9800. (9800, 9801)<ref>{{Cite web |last=Weisstein |first=Eric W. |title=Powerful Number |url=https://mathworld.wolfram.com/PowerfulNumber.html |access-date=2026-09-11 |website=mathworld.wolfram.com |publisher=Wolfram Research, Inc. |language=en}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |title=The Prime Glossary: powerful number |url=https://t5k.org/glossary/page.php?sort=PowerfulNumber |access-date=2026-09-11 |website=t5k.org}}</ref>
